title: Duchy of Athens
capsule: The Duchy of Athens was a Crusader state established in 1205 by the Burgundian knight Otto de la Roche following the Fourth Crusade's partition of the Byzantine Empire, covering Attica and Boeotia with the Acropolis as its ducal citadel. The de la Roche dynasty held power until 1308, after which Walter V of Brienne assumed the duchy; his attempt to dismiss and underpay the Catalan Company he had hired led to his defeat and death at the Battle of the Halmyros on 15 March 1311, handing the duchy to the Catalans. The Catalan Company ruled as vassals of the Crown of Aragon until the 1380s, when Navarrese and Florentine forces displaced them and the Acciaioli family of Florence assumed control. The Ottomans ended the duchy definitively with the fall of Athens in 1456–1458.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The duchy's core territory in Attica and Boeotia is well documented through Latin chronicles and Aragonese chancery records, though its variable extensions into Thessaly and the Morea are less precisely bounded.
